question.text: What is the maximum exposure limit that a single mutual fund scheme can have to a single company's equity shares, as per SEBI regulations?

answer.text: 10% of the NAV of the scheme
15% of the NAV of the scheme
5% of the NAV of the scheme
25% of the NAV of the scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p84), a scheme shall not invest more than 10% of its NAV in equity shares or equity-related instruments of any company, except for index/sector/industry-specific schemes. Page 82 separately supports the aggregate limit that across all schemes, a mutual fund cannot hold more than 10% of any company's paid-up capital carrying voting rights. The Trap: 15% is not the trustee-approval extension for single-company equity exposure under p83 — the 12% extension on p83 relates to debt issuer exposure, not equity. 5% and 25% are unsupported as the single-company equity NAV limit for an open-ended equity scheme. Note: The 10% per-company equity cap is subject to the express exception for index, sector and industry-specific schemes (p84), which by design replicate a benchmark or focus on a defined segment.
